guide.summary: OpenWeatherMap has no OAuth and no app registration. You sign up with an email address, receive an API key (APPID), and pass it in the appid query parameter on every request. Nothing your users need to connect exists here: your agent calls the API with your own key on their behalf. The real constraints are account-wide call limits shared by all your users and keys, the free plan being locked to api.openweathermap.org, and key suspension if you exceed limits and ignore the warning email.
auth_alternatives: API key (APPID): the only supported credential. Use one key held server-side by your agent, since weather data is not tied to an end user. The trade-off is that all usage across every key and product counts against your single account's limits, and there is no per-user consent or isolation.

reasons_to_bring_own: There is no OAuth app to build or borrow. You need your own OpenWeather account and API key, because the API key is the only credential.
No Composio toolkit or managed auth was found for this provider.
build_or_borrow.verdict: Skip OAuth entirely: OpenWeatherMap has none, so sign up, take the emailed API key, store it server-side, and have your agent call the API with it on behalf of all users.

prerequisites.text: An OpenWeather account created with an email address. The API key arrives in the confirmation email. No review, domain verification or privacy policy is mentioned as a prerequisite.

redirect_uri_rules: Not applicable: OpenWeatherMap has no OAuth app registration and publishes no OAuth or OpenID discovery document.

blockers.text: Call limits are enforced per account, combining every key and product. All of your agent's users share one quota.
blockers.workaround: Cache results and call each location no more than once every 10 minutes, as OpenWeather recommends. Move to a paid plan if free limits are not enough.

blockers.text: Exceeding the limit triggers a warning email, and the key is suspended if you do not respond.
blockers.workaround: Send the account email to a monitored inbox and respond promptly. When the limit is hit, retry after 10 minutes with the request unchanged.

app_specific_gotchas.text: There is no OAuth at all, so there is no per-user connect flow to build. Your agent uses one API key for everyone.
Adding more API keys does not add quota. Limits count total account usage across all keys and products.
The free plan only works against api.openweathermap.org. Paid plans move you to a different endpoint, sent in the confirmation or activation email, so the base URL must be configurable.
OpenWeather does not provide technical support for using its API key inside third-party applications. You are on your own if something breaks in your agent integration.
When rate limited, retry after 10 minutes with the exact same request so OpenWeather's caching service can serve it.

scope_tiers.purpose: Call OpenWeather weather APIs on behalf of the agent. There is no OAuth and no scopes; one key grants access to the weather APIs your plan includes.
scope_tiers.gate: No review, domain verification or privacy policy is described. The only gates are signing up with an email and staying inside the account-level call limits of your plan.

paths.verdict: Easy. This is not an OAuth integration. Sign up, take the API key from the confirmation email or the account page, and pass it as appid on every call. There is no app review. The only time you do not control is email delivery of the key, and no claim says how long that takes, so the total below excludes it. The real risks are the account-level call limits and the fact that OpenWeather does not give technical support for keys used inside third-party apps.

nodes.title: Sign up for an OpenWeather account with an email address
Receive the API key in the confirmation email (also listed on the account page). Delivery time is not documented.
Copy the key from the account page into the agent's secret store. Generate a separate key there if you want one per environment.
Write the integration: send every request to api.openweathermap.org on the free plan, with the key in the appid query parameter
Add per-location caching (at most one call per location every 10 minutes) and retry handling that waits 10 minutes and resends the request unchanged
Decide whether the free plan is enough or buy a paid plan. Paid plans use a different endpoint that arrives in the confirmation email.
Run a test call with the stored key and confirm data returns

paths.verdict: No review gate, but a policy cliff. There is no OAuth, so your users cannot connect their own OpenWeather accounts through a consent flow. Your two options are a shared key, where all users' usage is combined under your account's limits, or having each user paste their own key. OpenWeather does not give technical support for keys used in third-party apps. No publish toggle or admin approval is described. As with the internal path, key email delivery time is not documented and is not counted in the total.

steps.title: Confirm there is no OAuth app to register
steps.detail_md: OpenWeatherMap does not use OAuth. An API key (APPID) is the only credential needed (c1, c11, c24). Probes found no OpenID or OAuth discovery document on openweathermap.org (c33, c34). There is no client ID, client secret, redirect URI, scope list or app review to plan for. No Composio toolkit or managed auth was found for this provider, so you will wire it up yourself.

steps.title: Decide the credential model: one shared key or each user brings their own
steps.detail_md:
This is your call, and it changes who pays and who gets suspended.

- **Shared key (your account):** simplest for users. But call limits are counted per account, and usage from all keys and products is combined (c5, c13, c26). Plans set account-level daily and per-minute limits (c17). Every one of your users draws from the same pool.
- **User-supplied key:** each user signs up and pastes their own APPID, so each user's limits are separate. More friction at onboarding.

Also note: OpenWeather says it does not give technical support for using its key inside third-party applications (c10, c21), and one source phrases this as not supporting that use (c31). Read their terms yourself before shipping a shared key in a multi-user product. The provided material does not say whether this is a prohibition or only a support limit.

steps.title: Sign up for an OpenWeather account
steps.detail_md: Sign up with an email address at the account site. The home page redirects to the sign-in page (c32). No review, domain verification or privacy policy is listed as a prerequisite (c12).

steps.title: Receive the API key by confirmation email (wait not documented)
steps.detail_md: The free API key is sent in a confirmation email after sign-up (c2, c12, c22). How long this email takes is **not documented**. Treat the wait as unknown, not as instant. The key is also listed on the account page (c2, c23).

steps.title: Generate separate keys if you want them
steps.detail_md: More keys can be generated on the account page (c2, c23). Useful to separate dev and prod. Remember extra keys do not add capacity: limits are per account and all keys are combined (c5, c26).

steps.title: Write the integration code
steps.detail_md:
- Store the key as a secret (your env var or secrets manager); never put it in client-side code.
- Pass the key in the `appid` query parameter on every call (c4). Requests without a key are not processed (c3, c14, c25).
- On the free plan, call only `api.openweathermap.org` (c7, c15, c27). Keep the base host configurable, because paid plans get a different endpoint in their confirmation email (c7, c15, c27).
- If you chose user-supplied keys in step 2, add a field where the user pastes their APPID and a test call to validate it.

steps.title: Add per-location caching and limit-hit retry
steps.detail_md:
- Cache results per location for 10 minutes. OpenWeather recommends at most one call per location every 10 minutes because the model does not update more often (c6, c16, c28).
- When the limit is hit, retry after 10 minutes with the request unchanged so their caching service can handle it (c19).

This matters most with a shared key, since all your users share one account limit (c5).

steps.title: Watch the account inbox for over-limit notices
steps.detail_md: Going over the limit does not suspend the key immediately. An email is sent first, suggesting a paid plan, and the key is suspended if there is no response (c8, c18, c30). Make sure the sign-up email is a monitored address, not a personal inbox that nobody reads. The deadline for responding is not documented.

steps.title: Upgrade to a paid plan if free limits are not enough
steps.detail_md: Paid plans differ in included APIs, service level and calls per minute (c20, c29, c17). Prices and exact limits are not in the provided material. After paying, switch the base host to the endpoint given in the confirmation email (c7, c15, c27).

steps.title: Ship: no review or publish step
steps.detail_md: No app review is described (c11), no domain verification or privacy policy prerequisite is mentioned (c12), and no workspace admin approval or publish toggle is described (c31). Once the key works and caching is in place, the integration is shareable.

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: No, OpenWeatherMap does not offer an OAuth app-review process because it authenticates requests with a per-account API key rather than user OAuth consent, so any registered developer gets a key immediately.
belief_diff.finding: The claims state OpenWeather uses no OAuth, only an API key (APPID), with no app review described, and the OpenID and OAuth discovery endpoints return 404.

belief_diff.prior_belief: There is no approval wait; a new API key is typically activated within about 10 minutes of signup, though some keys can take up to 2 hours to become active.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say the key is sent by email after sign-up but give no activation timing; the 10-minute figure in the claims refers to the rate-limit retry advice, not key activation, and the 2-hour figure is not addressed.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: The free tier allows 60 calls per minute and 1,000,000 calls per month, and this applies identically to every new key with no separate unapproved restriction.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say limits are account-level, combined across all keys and products, and vary by plan, but give no specific numbers and do not mention an unapproved restriction.

belief_diff.prior_belief: The free plan requires no payment card, and paid subscriptions are optional for higher call volumes or additional endpoints.
belief_diff.finding: The claims describe a free plan reached by email sign-up and paid plans that differ in APIs, service level and calls per minute, with paid plans using a different endpoint; no payment card requirement is mentioned either way.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: No domain, privacy policy, demo video, or business verification is required; an email-verified account is sufficient to generate an API key.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say sign-up is by email with no review, domain verification or privacy policy mentioned as a prerequisite; demo video and business verification are not addressed.

belief_diff.prior_belief: OpenWeatherMap has no redirect URI setting because it issues no OAuth authorization flow, so none needs to be registered or validated.
belief_diff.finding: The claims state there is no OAuth at all and no OAuth app registration, which implies no redirect URI flow, though no claim explicitly mentions redirect URIs.
